training_history.opening: Mr. Kumar today. Fifty-two, stomach pain, and a terrible patient. Go on. Ask.

questions.ask: When did the pain start, and has it moved?
questions.answer: Last night, around my belly button. This morning it moved down here, low on the right.
questions.fact: Pain moved from belly button to low right
questions.why: Pain that starts at the belly button and moves low on the right is the classic story of appendicitis.

questions.ask: Are you allergic to anything?
questions.answer: Penicillin. I came up in a rash once. Big one.
questions.why: He's allergic to penicillin. The usual antibiotic before surgery would have given him a reaction on the table.

questions.ask: Do you take any medicines?
questions.answer: A blood thinner. For my heart. And something for acidity, when I remember.
questions.why: He takes a blood thinner. Operate without knowing and he bleeds, a lot.

questions.ask: When did you last eat or drink?
questions.answer: Breakfast at eight. Two idlis and tea. Is that bad?
questions.why: He ate at eight. A full stomach under anaesthetic can come back up into the lungs, so surgery has to wait.

questions.ask: Show me exactly where it hurts.
questions.answer: Here. Sharp when I walk, worse when I cough. Don't press it. Don't.
questions.fact: Sharp low right, worse on coughing

questions.ask: Have you had any operations before?
questions.answer: My tonsils. I was eight. I still remember the ice cream.

questions.ask: Do you smoke or drink?
questions.answer: I gave up smoking. Mostly. Weekends don't count.

questions.ask: Do you follow the cricket?
questions.answer: Who doesn't? That's one question gone, Doctor. Patients get tired. So do I.

questions.ask: Is it stressful at work?
questions.answer: I'm a bank manager. Everything is stressful. It's not why my belly hurts.

lakshmi_history.opening: Ask, Doctor. But quickly, before the next one comes. It comes every hour now.

questions.ask: Where is the pain, and when does it come?
questions.answer: Here, under my right ribs. After food, like a fist squeezing. It goes through to my back, up to my shoulder.
questions.fact: Pain under right ribs after meals, into the shoulder
questions.why: Pain under the right ribs after food, going through to the shoulder blade, is the gallbladder's story.

questions.ask: Do you take any medicines?
questions.answer: Metformin. For sugar. Please... my son doesn't know. Don't tell Arjun.
questions.fact: Diabetic, on metformin (her son doesn't know)
questions.why: She's diabetic. Her sugar has to be watched around surgery, and metformin is stopped before an anaesthetic.

questions.ask: Any fever or shivering?
questions.answer: Last night I was shaking under two blankets. In this heat!
questions.why: Fever with gallbladder pain means infection. That turns 'come back in six weeks' into 'treat her now'.

questions.ask: When did you last eat or drink?
questions.answer: Black tea at six. Only tea. I know what fried food does to me now.
questions.why: Black tea at six. Clear drinks are allowed until two hours before an anaesthetic; food waits six.

questions.ask: Has your urine or your skin changed colour?
questions.answer: My urine is dark. Like cola. My skin, I don't know. I don't look in mirrors at my age.

questions.ask: Are you allergic to anything?
questions.answer: Nothing. Only to my son's lectures.

questions.ask: Your son lives in Dubai?
questions.answer: Eleven years. He sends money and opinions. That was a question gone, Doctor.

questions.ask: Do you watch the nine o'clock serial?
questions.answer: Every night. It's not why my stomach hurts.

lakshmi_exam.opening: Gently, Doctor. It's been a long night.

spots.label: Eyes
spots.finding: A faint yellow tinge in the whites of her eyes.
spots.says: My neighbour said I look yellow. I said it's the tube light.
spots.fact: Whites of the eyes slightly yellow
spots.why: Yellow eyes can mean a stone has slipped into the main bile duct. It changes what scan she needs.

spots.label: Temperature
spots.finding: 37.9 degrees. A fever.
spots.why: She has a fever: an infected gallbladder needs antibiotics and surgery soon, not a list in six weeks.

spots.label: Pulse
spots.finding: Pulse 98, regular. A little fast.

spots.label: Lower left
spots.finding: Soft. Nothing here.

spots.label: Lower right
spots.finding: Soft, no pain. Not her appendix, then.

spots.label: Upper left
spots.finding: Soft. Nothing to learn here.

spots.label: Upper right
spots.finding: As you press under her ribs she breathes in and stops, mid-breath. Murphy's sign.
spots.says: Aah! Stop, stop. That's the place.
spots.fact: Catches her breath under the right ribs (Murphy's sign)
spots.why: Pressing under the right ribs while she breathed in stopped her short: Murphy's sign, the gallbladder.

diagnoses.why: Right: a stone blocking the gallbladder, now inflamed and infected. Antibiotics, then the gallbladder out.
Not the appendix: her lower right was soft. The pain lives under the ribs.
Worth thinking of in a diabetic, but the pain is pressed out of her right side, not her chest.
Gas doesn't give a fever or Murphy's sign. Sent home, she'd be back tonight, sicker.

kunal_exam.about: 24 · fell off his scooter, right wrist
kunal_exam.opening: Careful! This hand is worth more than your salary. I'm filming this, by the way.

spots.label: Move
spots.finding: He bends and straightens the wrist, wincing at the ends. His grip is strong.
spots.why: He moves it and grips hard. A badly broken wrist rarely lets you do either.

spots.label: Look
spots.finding: Mild swelling on the back of the wrist. No bend, no step. The bones are in line.
spots.why: Look first: no bend and no step. A badly broken wrist looks broken.

spots.label: Snuffbox
spots.finding: You press the hollow at the base of his thumb. He doesn't flinch.
spots.why: The hollow at the base of the thumb hides the scaphoid, a small bone that breaks quietly. His isn't tender.

spots.label: Pulse
spots.finding: A strong pulse at the wrist.

spots.label: Fingers
spots.finding: Warm and pink, and he feels you touch each one.

spots.label: Phone
spots.finding: He's filming you. That's not an examination.
spots.says: Say hi to my eleven thousand followers, Doctor.

diagnoses.why: Right. Swollen, but it moves, it grips, and the snuffbox isn't tender. A splint, ice and painkillers. Then home.
The scaphoid is the one to fear, but his snuffbox wasn't tender. If it were, he'd need a cast and a repeat X-ray.

diagnoses.text: A broken wrist that needs surgery
diagnoses.why: A badly broken wrist is bent and won't grip. His does both. No operation, whoever his uncle is.

rider_exam.opening: A passer-by brought him in. No helmet, no wallet. He's grey, Doctor. Where first?

spots.label: Airway
spots.finding: He groans when you speak to him. The airway is open.
spots.why: Airway always comes early: if he can groan, air is moving.

spots.label: Breathing
spots.finding: Fast, shallow breaths, both sides of the chest moving. Oxygen on.
spots.why: Both sides of his chest move, so no collapsed lung. Oxygen on and move on.

spots.label: Thigh
spots.finding: Bright red blood pumping from a gash in his right thigh. You lean on it with both hands.
spots.fact: Pumping bleed from the right thigh: pressure on
spots.why: His thigh was pumping blood. Hard pressure, early, keeps him alive until theatre.

spots.label: Pulse
spots.finding: Fast and thin at the wrist. 128.
spots.why: A fast, weak pulse means he has lost a lot of blood. He needs blood, not just fluids.

spots.label: Head
spots.finding: A graze on his scalp. His pupils react to your torch.

spots.label: Pocket
spots.finding: A cracked phone, buzzing. The screen says: Pooja calling.

diagnoses.text: A torn artery in the thigh
diagnoses.why: Right. A torn artery in the thigh: pressure now, blood on the way, theatre tonight.
The graze bleeds, but his pupils react and he's talking. The thigh is what's killing him.

diagnoses.text: Drunk. Let him sleep it off
diagnoses.why: He's grey because he's bleeding, not because he's drunk. Assume nothing at two in the morning.

joseph_exam.opening: Go ahead, young Doctor. I taught chemistry for thirty-eight years. I can bear a little prodding.

spots.label: Look
spots.finding: His belly is swollen like a drum. An old scar runs down the middle.
spots.says: That? 1987. They took out a bit of my bowel. I kept the rest.
spots.why: An old scar means old surgery, and old surgery leaves bands inside that can kink the bowel: adhesions.

spots.label: Listen
spots.finding: High-pitched tinkling, like water dripping in a pipe.
spots.why: Tinkling sounds mean the bowel is blocked and straining to push past it.

spots.label: Press
spots.finding: Tight, but soft. Sore all over, no one sharp spot.
spots.fact: Tense but soft, no sharp spot

spots.label: Groins
spots.finding: No lump in either groin. Not a trapped hernia.
spots.says: At my age, Doctor, nothing down there surprises me.
spots.why: A trapped hernia in the groin is the other common cause. Always look, however shy the patient.

spots.label: Pulse
spots.finding: Pulse 92, regular.

spots.label: Eyes
spots.finding: His eyes twinkle. That's not a medical finding.
spots.says: Looking for something, Doctor? My reading glasses are on the locker.

diagnoses.text: Bowel blocked by old scar bands (adhesions)
diagnoses.why: Right. Old surgery, a drum-tight belly, tinkling sounds and no hernia: adhesions. A tube and a drip often settle it.
Constipation doesn't make you vomit green or tinkle like a pipe. This is a blockage.
It happens at 81, and a scan will check, but with his scar, adhesions come first. Don't frighten him before you know.

aarav_scan.opening: Aarav's film. Something round in his gullet. Take your time and tell me what it is.

lines.zoom: Look at the edge. Two rings, one inside the other. A halo.
lines.side: From the side it has a step in it. Coins don't have steps.
lines.missed_zoom: You never looked closely: a battery shows a double ring, a halo, at its edge.
lines.missed_side: You never turned to the side view: a battery has a step in it, a coin is one flat line.

answers.text: A coin. It can wait until morning.
answers.why: From the front a battery and a coin look alike. The halo and the step say battery, and waiting would burn through his gullet.

answers.text: A button battery. It comes out now.
answers.why: Right: a button battery. It can burn through the gullet in two hours. Endoscopy, now.
There is something there: the round white shadow in his gullet.

teaching_scan.opening: A teaching film. Ishaan, four, swallowed something at a wedding. Read it properly.

lines.zoom: One clean edge. No second ring.
lines.side: From the side, one thin flat line.
lines.missed_zoom: You never looked closely at the edge: one clean ring is a coin.
lines.missed_side: You never turned to the side view: a coin is one flat line.

answers.why: Right: one clean edge and a flat line from the side. A coin. Most pass on their own.
No halo and no step: it's a coin. Better safe than sorry, but read the film before you call for an endoscopy.
There is something there: a round white shadow in his gullet.

deepa_history.opening: Ask, Doctor. But the lunch rush starts at twelve, and Babu can't make dal.

questions.ask: How did it happen, and when?
questions.answer: A big glass bowl of raita slipped. I caught it. Stupid. An hour ago, not more.
questions.fact: Glass bowl broke in her hand, under an hour ago
questions.why: A fresh wound can be closed today. And broken glass means there may still be glass inside.

questions.ask: Can you move every finger, and feel me touch each one?
questions.answer: They all move. See? The little one feels a bit fuzzy. No. It's fine. Mostly.
questions.fact: Moves every finger, feeling mostly normal
questions.why: Movement and feeling tell you whether a tendon or a nerve is cut, before you go looking inside.

questions.ask: When did you last have a tetanus injection?
questions.answer: Tetanus? In school. Twenty years ago? I was in a green pinafore.
questions.fact: Last tetanus jab about twenty years ago
questions.why: A dirty kitchen wound and twenty years since the last jab: she needs a booster today.

questions.ask: Which hand do you write and chop with?
questions.answer: The right. Of course it's the right.

questions.ask: Are you allergic to anything?
questions.answer: Only to Babu.

questions.ask: Do you take any medicines?
questions.answer: Iron tablets, when I remember. I don't remember.

questions.ask: Is the dal makhani at your dhaba good?
questions.answer: Best on Station Road. Not a medical question, Doctor.

questions.ask: Is someone here with you?
questions.answer: My husband's at the gas agency. He faints at blood. Better he stays there.

bansal_exam.about: 67 · 'kidney stone', back pain into the groin
bansal_exam.opening: Gently, Doctor. The tablets helped, a little. Then they stopped helping.

spots.label: Face
spots.finding: Grey and sweaty. Cold to touch. He looks sicker than a man with a stone should.
spots.says: Is it hot in here? I'm cold. I'm hot. Both.

spots.label: Pressure, pulse
spots.finding: 92 over 58, and a pulse of 116, fast and thready. His notes say he's had high blood pressure for twenty years.
spots.fact: Blood pressure 92/58 in a man who runs high, pulse 116
spots.why: Low pressure and a racing pulse in a man who usually runs high: he's losing blood somewhere you can't see. That's shock.

spots.label: Above the navel
spots.finding: A mass above his navel that pushes your two hands apart with every heartbeat. It pulses, and it swells.
spots.says: Ohh. That's the place. That's where the knife is.
spots.fact: A pulsating, expanding mass above the navel
spots.why: A mass that pushes your hands apart with each beat is a swollen aorta. With low pressure, it's leaking.

spots.label: Groin pulses
spots.finding: The pulses in both groins are weak.
spots.why: Weak pulses in both groins: the blood isn't getting past the aorta. The trouble is upstream, in his belly.

spots.label: Kidney
spots.finding: Over his right kidney from the side: sore, but no worse than anywhere else. A stone usually makes this spot sing.

diagnoses.why: Right: a pulsating mass, low pressure, fast pulse, a smoker over sixty. His aorta is leaking. Vascular surgeons, blood, now.
A first 'kidney stone' in a man over sixty is an aneurysm until you've felt his belly. His pressure was falling.
Back strain doesn't drop the blood pressure or put a pulse in the belly.
His lower right was soft. The pain was in his back and the middle of his belly.

farida_history.opening: Ask away, Doctor. I make my students show their working. You can show yours.

questions.ask: Tell me about the pain attacks.
questions.answer: A year of them. After samosas, mostly. Under my right ribs, then through to my back. The scan showed stones.
questions.fact: A year of gallstone attacks after fatty food
questions.why: A year of attacks with stones on the scan is why she needs the gallbladder out.

questions.ask: Do you take any medicines? Even ones you buy yourself?
questions.answer: Only aspirin, for headaches. I took one this morning, in fact. Forty exam papers will do that.
questions.why: Aspirin thins the blood for days. The team needs to know, so they're ready if the liver bed oozes.

questions.ask: Are you allergic to anything?
questions.answer: Nothing. I've checked. I'm a chemist.
questions.why: Now the time-out can confirm 'none known' honestly, because somebody actually asked her.

questions.ask: When did you last eat or drink?
questions.answer: Dinner at eight last night. Two sips of water at six.
questions.why: Properly fasted: no food for six hours, clear water up to two hours before.

questions.ask: Have you ever turned yellow, or had dark urine?
questions.answer: Never. My skin is this colour by birth, thank you.

questions.ask: Any operations before?
questions.answer: Two caesareans. My children are fourteen and eleven, and louder than Class Ten.

questions.ask: What do you teach?
questions.answer: Chemistry. Twenty years, three lost eyebrows. Not mine.

questions.ask: Have you read about keyhole surgery?
questions.answer: Far too much. Next question, please.

raju_history.about: 38 · stuck lump in the left groin
raju_history.opening: Ask fast, Doctor. Please. It's burning.

questions.ask: Tell me about the lump.
questions.answer: Two years it's been there. It always went back when I lay down. Last night, lifting cement, it came out and stayed.
questions.fact: Hernia for two years, stuck since last night
questions.why: A hernia that suddenly won't go back, with pain, is trapped. The bowel inside can lose its blood supply.

questions.ask: When did you last eat?
questions.answer: A paratha at five. Then I went to the site. Then this.
questions.why: He ate a few hours ago: a full stomach can come up into his lungs under anaesthetic. Dr. Khan must know.

questions.ask: Have you been sick? Opened your bowels?
questions.answer: Sick three times. Green. Nothing out the other end since yesterday.
questions.why: Vomiting and nothing passing means the bowel is blocked where it's trapped.

questions.ask: Are you allergic to anything?
questions.answer: No. Only to my contractor.
questions.why: Asked, so the time-out's 'none known' is the truth and not a guess.

questions.ask: Do you take any medicines?
questions.answer: Nothing. I'm strong like a buffalo. Was.

questions.ask: What work do you do?
questions.answer: Bricks. Cement bags. Fifty kilos each, all day.

questions.ask: Did you watch the match last night?
questions.answer: India lost. That's when the lump came out, I think. Coincidence?

questions.ask: Shall we call someone for you?
questions.answer: My wife. But don't say 'hospital'. Say 'Raju is fine'.

gomes_history.about: 81 · fell at home, broken left hip
gomes_history.opening: Eh? Speak up, child. Everyone in this hospital whispers. Is it a library?

questions.ask: What happened when you fell?
questions.answer: I got up in the night for the bathroom. My head went swimmy, and then the floor was in my face. I didn't trip. I know my own floor.
questions.fact: Went dizzy at night, then fell. Didn't trip
questions.why: Dizzy first, then a fall: something made her faint. Her heart and her tablets need looking at, not only her hip.

questions.ask: Which tablets do you take every day?
questions.answer: The blood thinner. Warfarin, for my heart's flutter. A water tablet. A little heart one. I take them all, every day, like a good girl.
questions.fact: Takes warfarin for an irregular heartbeat, a water tablet and digoxin
questions.why: Warfarin thins her blood. It has to be stopped and reversed before the operation, or she bleeds.

questions.ask: Do you usually wear a hearing aid?
questions.answer: In my handbag. The black one, there. Put it in for me? ...Ah. Now you can stop shouting, and I can stop guessing.
questions.fact: Deaf without her hearing aid. Not confused
questions.why: She isn't confused. She's deaf. With her hearing aid in, she can understand you and make her own decisions.

questions.ask: Are you allergic to anything?
questions.answer: Penicillin. I came up in a rash like a map of Goa. Nineteen seventy-eight. I remember because it was Francis's first birthday.
questions.why: A penicillin allergy changes the antibiotic in theatre. It only counts if somebody asks.

questions.ask: Who is at home with you?
questions.answer: Nobody. My husband died eleven years ago. Francis lives in Pune. He phones on Sundays. Mostly.
questions.fact: Lives alone. Her son lives in Pune

questions.ask: When did you last eat or drink?
questions.answer: Toast at seven, before the ambulance. With butter. Don't tell my doctor.

questions.ask: Where does it hurt?
questions.answer: My hip, child. The one pointing the wrong way. That's why the young man put me on this trolley.

questions.ask: Are you from Goa?
questions.answer: Margao. Born there, married there, and buried there one day. Not today, I hope.

brief.easy: I wrote Mrs. Gomes's chart at three in the morning. Dr. Iyer says check it together. A couple of lines don't feel right to me.
brief.hard: Mrs. Gomes's chart. I wrote it at three in the morning, after the second admission. Please check everything.
brief.extreme: Her chart. I wrote it at three. I think it's fine? It's probably fine. Dr. Iyer said you'd check it anyway.

gomes_chart.half: That line is wrong, you're right. But not for that reason. Look again at why.
gomes_chart.no_more: I can't see anything else wrong with it. Sign it, if you agree.

signed.all: Fixed, every one. I'm writing these down on the back of my hand. Thank you for not shouting.
signed.some: Fixed what we found. I'll check the rest again before the drug round. Twice.
signed.none: Signed. Okay. I hope that's okay.

ok.when: Stopped for surgery · INR at 6 am
ok.defend: I stopped her warfarin and gave vitamin K, so her blood clots in time for theatre. That one I knew.

wrong.found: Her INR is 2.8 and she's in theatre today. I copied her list from home. Stopping it, and vitamin K.
wrong.why: Warfarin thins the blood. With an INR of 2.8 and surgery today, it stops, and she gets vitamin K.
wrong.hint: Look at her INR. Then look at the theatre list.

ok.defend: Micrograms, not milligrams. I wrote the word out in full, the way Sister Grace taught me.

wrong.found: Milligrams. A thousand times the dose. That would have stopped her heart. I need to sit down.
wrong.why: Digoxin is dosed in micrograms. 62.5 mg is a thousand times too much. Always write 'micrograms' in full.
wrong.hint: Read every unit on that chart out loud.

ok.defend: She's allergic to penicillin, so not co-amoxiclav. Clindamycin. I checked with pharmacy.

wrong.found: Co-amoxiclav is a penicillin. And her allergy is right there at the top of the chart. In red.
wrong.why: Co-amoxiclav contains a penicillin, and she's allergic. Read the allergy box before every antibiotic.
wrong.hint: Read the allergy box. Then read every antibiotic.

ok.defend: For constipation. Morphine and a broken hip, she'll need it. By mouth, twice a day.

wrong.found: Into a vein? It's a syrup! I ticked the wrong box at three in the morning. That's not an excuse. I know.
wrong.why: Lactulose is a syrup, taken by mouth. The wrong route can be as dangerous as the wrong drug.
wrong.hint: How do you take a syrup?

ok.defend: Half a gram, because she's only forty-two kilos. Under fifty, the usual gram is too much.

wrong.found: She's forty-two kilos. The full adult dose is for people over fifty. Her liver would have paid for it.
wrong.why: Under 50 kg, paracetamol comes down: a gram four times a day is too much for a 42 kg woman's liver.
wrong.hint: Check her weight against every dose.

ok.defend: A small dose, not too often. She's eighty-one with tired kidneys, so it would build up.

wrong.found: Ten milligrams every two hours, at eighty-one, with poor kidneys. She'd stop breathing by morning.
wrong.why: Old age and weak kidneys let morphine build up. Start small, not too often, and watch her breathing.
wrong.hint: Eighty-one, with poor kidneys. Which painkiller builds up?

ok.defend: The lower dose, because of her kidneys. And not until after the operation.

wrong.found: Her kidneys can't clear the full dose. Forty would build up and she could bleed. Twenty, then.
wrong.why: Enoxaparin is cleared by the kidneys. With an eGFR under 30, the dose drops to 20 mg.
wrong.hint: Which of her drugs do the kidneys have to clear?

ok.defend: A water tablet, so it's the morning. Otherwise she's up all night for the bathroom.

wrong.found: A water tablet at night. She'd be up for the bathroom at two in the morning. That's how she fell.
wrong.why: Water tablets go in the morning. At night, an 81-year-old who falls walks to the bathroom in the dark.
wrong.hint: Think about what each tablet does in the night.

nanda_exam.about: 58 · two days after a bowel operation
nanda_exam.opening: Just sore, Doctor. Dr. Sethi said sore is normal. Is sore supposed to move about like this?

spots.label: Pulse, temperature
spots.finding: Pulse 112 and bounding. At eight it was 88. Temperature 38.4.
spots.why: A pulse climbing hour by hour after bowel surgery is often the first sign of a leak, before the belly says much.

spots.label: Chest
spots.finding: Breathing a little fast, 22 a minute. Clear on both sides.

spots.label: Wound
spots.finding: The dressing is dry. The wound itself looks clean.

spots.label: Press the belly
spots.finding: Tender everywhere now, not just round the wound. He goes rigid when you press, and worse when you let go.
spots.says: Aah! Everywhere. Since about nine, it's everywhere.
spots.fact: Tender all over, rigid, worse on letting go
spots.why: Pain spreading from the wound to the whole belly, worse when you let go: the belly's lining is inflamed. Something is leaking.

spots.label: Catheter bag
spots.finding: Forty millilitres in the bag since eight. Dark, like strong tea.
spots.fact: Only 40 ml of urine in three hours
spots.why: Hardly any urine: his kidneys aren't getting enough blood. He's sliding into septic shock.

spots.label: Eyes
spots.finding: Tired eyes. No yellow in them.
spots.says: My wife says I look terrible. She's right, as usual.

diagnoses.text: A leak from the bowel join
diagnoses.why: Right: two days after a bowel join, a racing pulse, a fever, pain spreading everywhere and no urine. The join is leaking. Fluids, antibiotics and his surgeon, tonight.
Normal pain stays round the wound and eases each day. His spread, his pulse climbed and his kidneys slowed.
His chest was clear. The trouble was in his belly.
A clot makes you breathless with a soft belly. His belly was rigid and his urine dried up.

imran_exam.opening: Imran Ali, twenty-four. Fell two floors off the scaffold at the new mall site. His friends carried him in. He's very pale, Doctor.

spots.label: Airway
spots.finding: He answers you in a whisper. The airway is open.
spots.says: My side... it's my side, Doctor...
spots.why: If he can talk, his airway is open. Check it first anyway, every time.

spots.label: Breathing
spots.finding: Both sides move, but he catches his breath on the left. Ribs crunch under your fingers, low on the left.
spots.fact: Broken ribs, low on the left
spots.why: Broken lower left ribs sit right over the spleen. When they break, it can tear underneath.

spots.label: Pulse
spots.finding: Fast and thin at the wrist. 132. His hands are cold.
spots.why: A fast weak pulse and cold hands: he has lost a lot of blood somewhere you can't see.

spots.label: Pelvis
spots.finding: You press gently on both hips. The pelvis is stable.

spots.label: Upper left belly
spots.finding: The upper left of his belly is tense and swelling under your hand. He groans, and pulls his left shoulder up.
spots.says: Aah! And my shoulder. Why does my shoulder hurt?
spots.fact: Upper left belly tense and swelling, pain in the left shoulder
spots.why: A swelling upper left belly with pain in the left shoulder tip means blood under the diaphragm. The spleen.

spots.label: Head
spots.finding: A lump on his forehead. Pupils equal and reacting. He knows where he is.

diagnoses.why: Right. Broken left ribs, a swelling upper left belly, pain in the shoulder tip and shock: his spleen has burst. Blood, and theatre, now.
Broken ribs hurt, but they don't push the pulse to 132. Something under them is bleeding.
He's alert, with equal pupils. His belly is where the blood is going.
He moves all four limbs and feels everything. The danger is in his belly.

kurup_history.about: 64 · vomiting, belly swollen like a drum
kurup_history.opening: Doctor. Good. Please make it stop. I've been sick in two buses and a lift.

questions.ask: When did the vomiting start?
questions.answer: Saturday night. Green, then worse. And my belly's gone tight as a drum. Even the fan sounds hollow.
questions.fact: Vomiting for two days, belly swollen and tight
questions.why: Vomiting with a swollen, tight belly: the bowel is blocked somewhere.

questions.ask: Have you passed any wind, or opened your bowels?
questions.answer: Nothing since Friday. Not even, forgive me, a whisper.
questions.fact: No wind or stool since Friday
questions.why: Nothing out at all means a complete blockage. It won't settle with a drip and patience.

questions.ask: Have you had an operation on your belly before?
questions.answer: Twenty-two years ago. My gallbladder, open, here. In this very hospital. A young surgeon with a very serious moustache.
questions.fact: Open gallbladder operation in this hospital, 2004
questions.why: Old belly operations leave scar bands, the commonest cause of a blocked bowel. And her old notes are in this building.

questions.ask: Any trouble with your chest or breathing?
questions.answer: Asthma, since the cashew factory. Two inhalers, the brown and the blue. Stairs make me whistle like a kettle.
questions.fact: Asthma, two inhalers, breathless on stairs
questions.why: Weak lungs change the anaesthetic. The anaesthetist needs to know before she's asleep, not after.

questions.ask: Are you allergic to anything?
questions.answer: Sticking plasters. Not medicines, plasters. I come up in squares, exactly the size of the plaster.

questions.ask: Which medicines do you take?
questions.answer: The two inhalers. A pressure tablet. And a sleeping tablet my daughter doesn't know about. Don't tell her.
questions.fact: Inhalers, a blood pressure tablet, a sleeping tablet

questions.ask: When did you last eat or drink?
questions.answer: Sips of water since Saturday. Everything comes back up. I'm sixty-four and I've become a fountain.

questions.ask: Where does it hurt?
questions.answer: All round the middle, in waves. Like the bus to Ernakulam. Stop, start, stop, start.

questions.ask: Who came in with you?
questions.answer: Venu, my husband. He's in the car park, losing an argument with the ticket machine.

brief.easy: Six off the bus so far. Tag them: red now, yellow soon, green walks, black beyond help. The rules are on the card. Use them, in order.
brief.hard: Eight here and the ambulances are queuing. Red, yellow, green, black. You know the order. Don't let the loud ones choose for you.
brief.extreme: Ten of them, two of us. I can't check your tags, Doctor. Trust the rules, not your eyes.

tagged.yellow: Yellow. {who} can wait, but not long.
tagged.green: Green. To the gate, please, and wait for a nurse.

sent.all: Every tag right. The trauma bay says it's the tidiest line they've ever had off a crash.
sent.some: Sending them in. Dr. Iyer will check the tags again inside.
sent.under: Sending them in. Doctor, one of the ones you tagged to wait is going grey. Dr. Iyer's pulling them forward.

casualties.looks: Shouting at everyone. Blood all over his face from a cut on his head.
casualties.walks: He storms over to the kerb, still shouting. Heads bleed like taps. He'll keep.

casualties.looks: Sitting very still against the bus wheel. She says she's fine. Very quietly.
casualties.stays: She tries. Her legs fold under her.
casualties.why: Breathing over thirty is red, however calm she sounds. Quiet isn't the same as fine.

casualties.looks: Slumped over the wheel. Not moving.
casualties.stays: No answer at all.
casualties.why: He wasn't breathing until you opened his airway, then he was. That's red, and every second counts.

casualties.looks: Holding her wrist and crying for her mother.
casualties.walks: She walks to the kerb, still holding her wrist. Probably broken. Definitely walking.

casualties.looks: Lying on the road, grey and sweaty. Says he's only a bit tired.
casualties.stays: He can't get up. He says he'll just rest here.
casualties.why: A nail bed slow to pink up means he's bleeding somewhere you can't see. That's red.

casualties.who: Young man with a bent leg
casualties.looks: His shin is bent the wrong way. He's swearing at the sky, loudly, in three languages.
casualties.stays: He can't put weight on it. He tells you so, at length.

casualties.looks: Lying in the road, eyes half open, not moving.
casualties.stays: No answer.

casualties.looks: Sitting on the kerb, staring. Not a scratch on him. He hasn't said a word.
casualties.stays: He doesn't get up when you ask. He doesn't seem to hear you.
casualties.why: He couldn't follow a simple command: a head injury until proven otherwise. Red.

casualties.looks: Holding his ribs. Every breath makes him wince.
casualties.stays: He tries, gasps, and sits back down.
casualties.why: Over thirty breaths a minute is red: broken ribs, and a lung that's struggling under them.

casualties.looks: Pulled out from under the seats a minute ago. Pale. Very polite.
casualties.stays: His legs won't hold him. He says sorry for the fuss.
casualties.why: Over two seconds for the nail bed to pink up: he's losing blood somewhere. Red.

casualties.looks: Sitting on her bag, very calm, asking if anyone has seen her spectacles.

casualties.looks: A cut across her forehead. Shouting for her son, Rehan.
casualties.walks: She's already up, looking under every seat for her son.

casualties.looks: Sitting up, dazed, one headphone still in. Blood trickling from his ear.
casualties.stays: He stands, sways, and sits down hard.

casualties.looks: Lying very still beside a bent bicycle. Breathing slowly, and noisily.
casualties.stays: Nothing. He snores.
casualties.why: Slow, noisy breathing and no response to a command: his brain is in trouble. Red.

sinha_history.about: 52 · fever, belly pain, gallbladder out on Saturday
sinha_history.opening: Ask, Doctor. In whole sentences, please. I've had two days of leaflets.

questions.ask: When was your operation, and what was done?
questions.answer: Saturday morning. Keyhole, my gallbladder, Dr. Sethi. I was home by six with a leaflet and a sandwich.
questions.fact: Keyhole gallbladder on Saturday, home the same evening
questions.why: Pain and fever days after a gallbladder operation means a leak or an infection inside until proven otherwise.

questions.ask: Where is the pain, and is it getting worse?
questions.answer: Under my ribs on the right, and now everywhere. Worse every hour. The leaflet said some pain is normal, so I waited.
questions.fact: Pain spreading from the right side to the whole belly, worse each hour
questions.why: Pain that spreads and keeps worsening isn't wound pain. Something is irritating the whole belly.

questions.ask: Have you had a fever, or shivers?
questions.answer: Shaking under two blankets last night. My son took my temperature on the phone, by shouting instructions. Thirty-nine.
questions.why: Fever and shivers mean infection. With bile loose in the belly, she can turn septic quickly.

questions.ask: Are you allergic to anything?
questions.answer: Penicillin. I swell up like a balloon at a wedding. I told them on Saturday. I think. Saturday was very fast.
questions.fact: Allergic to penicillin: she swells up
questions.why: The usual antibiotic for a belly operation, co-amoxiclav, is a penicillin. Theatre must know before she's asleep.

questions.ask: Have your eyes or skin turned yellow?
questions.answer: My son says my eyes look like old piano keys. A little yellow, he says. He's very poetic for a lawyer.

questions.ask: What colour is your urine?
questions.answer: Dark. Like strong tea. And not much of it, Doctor, since you ask so politely.

questions.ask: When did you last eat or drink?
questions.answer: Toast, yesterday morning. Sips of water since. Even the water argues with me.
questions.fact: Nothing but sips since yesterday morning

questions.ask: What did Dr. Sethi say after the operation?
questions.answer: 'Textbook.' Twice. Then he ran. He had a presentation, he said. With slides.

questions.ask: What do you do?
questions.answer: I taught Hindi at the girls' school for thirty-one years. I can silence a room with one eyebrow.

brief.easy: Life and limb cover. Six patients, three pairs of hands. Every bed gets a name, and the rules are on the card. I walk out at eight, Doctor. Make it so I can.
brief.hard: Eight patients, four of you, and Ananya is a student. I'll read it when you sign, not before. Then I'm on the gate with a placard.
brief.extreme: Ten patients. Five of you, counting your intern. No card and no help from me. I've already got my placard in my hand.

warn.student: {staff} is a student. {who} is too much for her on her own.

cb_banerjee_history.about: 79 · deep cut on the right forearm, broken glass bowl
cb_banerjee_history.opening: Ask, beta. I've brought biscuits for after. Only for good questions.

questions.ask: How did you cut it, and where did the glass land?
questions.answer: Making payesh. The bowl slipped, I grabbed it, and it broke in my hand. Milk, rice and glass all over the kitchen floor.
questions.fact: Cut on a broken bowl, glass on the kitchen floor
questions.why: Glass from a kitchen floor can hide in a wound with dirt behind it. It must be looked into and washed out, not just closed.

questions.ask: When did you last have a tetanus injection?
questions.answer: Tetanus? When my husband was alive. Twenty years? He stepped on a nail, and they did us both. Very romantic.
questions.fact: Last tetanus jab about twenty years ago
questions.why: A dirty wound and a tetanus jab twenty years old: she needs a booster today, whatever the board says.

questions.ask: Can you move all your fingers, and feel them all?
questions.answer: All five wiggle, all five feel. Watch. I knit with these, Doctor. I'd know.
questions.fact: All fingers move and feel normally
questions.why: A deep forearm cut can catch a tendon or a nerve. Fingers that move and feel mean stitches are enough.

questions.ask: Which medicines do you take?
questions.answer: A pressure tablet, and calcium that tastes of chalk. No blood thinners. Dr. Iyer asked me that last time. I remembered.
questions.fact: Blood pressure tablet and calcium, no blood thinners

questions.ask: How much did it bleed?
questions.answer: Two tea towels. I pressed it all night with the good one. My neighbour drove me in at six.
questions.fact: Bled into two towels, pressed overnight

questions.ask: Who is at home with you?
questions.answer: Nobody, since my husband. And a cat who belongs to the whole building. The neighbours check on me. Too often.

questions.ask: Do you still listen to the radio?
questions.answer: Every night. Forty years a radio officer on ships. I still listen to the weather at sea. Nobody else in my building does.

questions.ask: How are the grandchildren?
questions.answer: Six of them, and I knit for all six. The eldest wants to be a doctor. I told him to wash his hands.

cb_dev_history.about: 15 · pain low on the right since last night
cb_dev_history.opening: Ask me, not Papa. He'll tell you about parking.

questions.ask: Where did the pain start, and where is it now?
questions.answer: Round my belly button, last night after dinner. Then it moved down here, on the right. Now it's stabbing.
questions.fact: Pain from the belly button, moved low on the right
questions.why: Pain that starts at the belly button and moves low on the right is the classic story of appendicitis.

questions.ask: Does it hurt more when you move, cough, or go over bumps?
questions.answer: Every bump in the car. Mama hit all of them. I think on purpose.
questions.why: Pain on every bump means the lining of the belly is inflamed. The appendix is angry, and close to bursting.

questions.ask: Are you allergic to any medicines?
questions.answer: Penicillin. I came out in a rash all over when I was nine. Papa keeps it on a card in his wallet. Behind the important cards.
questions.fact: Allergic to penicillin: a rash all over
questions.why: The usual antibiotic for this operation, co-amoxiclav, is a penicillin. Theatre must know before he's asleep.

questions.ask: When did you last eat or drink?
questions.answer: Dinner at eight. Dal and rice. I was sick at midnight, so technically nothing. Some water at six.
questions.fact: Dinner at eight last night, sips of water at six

questions.ask: Have you been sick, or felt hot?
questions.answer: Sick once, in Mama's car. And I'm hot and cold at the same time. Is that normal?

questions.ask: Do you take any medicines?
questions.answer: Vitamins. Mama's vitamins. She stands there until I swallow them.

questions.ask: What are you studying?
questions.answer: Tenth standard. Board exams in March. Papa says this is an excellent opportunity to revise in bed.

questions.ask: Do you play any sport?
questions.answer: Cricket. Wicketkeeper. That's why I thought it was a ball in the stomach. It wasn't.

cb_tom_history.about: 41 · groin lump that won't go back
cb_tom_history.opening: Go on, then. I've heard you ask a hundred of these. Let's see if you were listening.

questions.ask: When did the lump appear, and does it go back in?
questions.answer: Six months ago, after I lifted the big orthopaedic tray. It used to go back when I lay down. Since last night it won't, and it's hard.
questions.fact: Groin lump for six months, stuck since last night
questions.why: A hernia that won't go back can trap bowel and cut off its blood. That makes it urgent: today, not next week.

questions.ask: When did you last eat?
questions.answer: A samosa at five, from the canteen, at the end of the night shift. Two samosas. It was a long night.
questions.fact: Ate two samosas at five this morning
questions.why: A full stomach can come up into the lungs under anaesthetic. Dr. Khan needs to know, so she can protect his airway.

questions.ask: Have you been sick, or stopped passing wind?
questions.answer: Sick once, at the bus stop. And no wind since midnight, which for a man of my habits is unusual.
questions.fact: Vomited once, no wind since midnight
questions.why: Vomiting and no wind with a stuck hernia: the bowel inside is blocked. It can't wait for a list.

questions.ask: Which side is it?
questions.answer: The left. Don't let anyone write right on the board. I've been the one fixing that board for twenty years.

questions.ask: Are you allergic to anything?
questions.answer: Nothing. I've handled every drug in this building for twenty years. Not one rash.

questions.ask: Do you take any medicines?
questions.answer: Antacids. From the cupboard in theatre. I'll replace them.

questions.ask: Who's been scrubbing in your place?
questions.answer: Neha. She moves my trays. She says she's improving them. She's wrong.

questions.ask: How long have you worked here?
questions.answer: Twenty years in March. Forty thousand swabs, roughly. I counted the first ten thousand properly.

cb_salim_history.about: 36 · came off his bike in the crash, pressure falling
cb_salim_history.brief: Four questions. His pressure is falling. Find out what would hurt him on the table, fast.

questions.ask: Where does it hurt?
questions.answer: Under my ribs on the left. And the tip of my left shoulder. I didn't land on my shoulder.
questions.fact: Pain under the left ribs and in the left shoulder tip
questions.why: Shoulder-tip pain after a blow to the left side means blood under the diaphragm, from the spleen. He's bleeding inside.

questions.ask: What did you hit, and how hard?
questions.answer: The divider. The bus pushed my bike, and my side hit the concrete. I heard something go. My bike made the same noise.
questions.fact: Left side into a concrete divider
questions.why: A hard blow to the lower left ribs is how a spleen tears.

questions.ask: Are you allergic to any medicines?
questions.answer: No. Nothing. Pooja is allergic to cats. Does that help?
questions.why: In a rush nobody asks, and then the time-out has to guess. Ask, and the board can be confirmed.

questions.ask: Do you feel dizzy, or thirsty?
questions.answer: So thirsty. And the ceiling moves when I move my head. Also when I don't.

questions.ask: When did you last eat?
questions.answer: Tea and a bun at seven. I was going to eat properly at lunch.
questions.fact: Tea and a bun at seven

questions.ask: Do you take any medicines?
questions.answer: Only painkillers for my old leg, now and then. Pooja counts them.
questions.fact: Painkillers now and then for an old leg injury

questions.ask: Who should we call?
questions.answer: Pooja's school. She's ten now. Don't frighten her. Call her teacher. The teacher is calmer than me.

questions.ask: What do you deliver?
questions.answer: Food. Biryani, mostly. Forty orders a day. The app gives me stars. I have four point nine.

cb_mehra_history.about: 79 · broken left hip, a fall at breakfast
cb_mehra_history.opening: Ask your questions. My son will phone in the middle of them. Ignore him. I do.

questions.ask: What medicines do you take, especially anything that thins the blood?
questions.answer: Warfarin, for my heart's rhythm. I took it last night, like always. My son counts them.
questions.fact: On warfarin, last dose last night
questions.why: Warfarin thins the blood. Her clotting must be checked and corrected before the cut, or she'll bleed.

questions.ask: Are you allergic to any medicines?
questions.answer: Penicillin. My throat closed once, in nineteen seventy-eight. I remember the year. I remember the doctor's tie.
questions.fact: Allergic to penicillin: her throat closed
questions.why: The usual antibiotic for a hip, co-amoxiclav, is a penicillin. Theatre must use another.

questions.ask: How did you fall? Did you black out or feel dizzy first?
questions.answer: I slipped on the bathroom tiles. I didn't faint. I remember every second, and the language I used.
questions.fact: Slipped on wet tiles, no blackout
questions.why: A fall from a faint means the heart or the brain needs looking at first. A slip means the hip is the whole story.

questions.ask: Where is the pain?
questions.answer: The left hip. And my pride.

questions.ask: When did you last eat?
questions.answer: Half a toast at seven. The other half is still on the plate, waiting for me.

questions.ask: Who is at home with you?
questions.answer: My son, his wife, and a cook who does everything better than both of them.

questions.ask: How is your son?
questions.answer: On the phone. Always on the phone.

questions.ask: What do you do all day?
questions.answer: I sit on three committees and ruin all of them.

cb_verghese_history.about: 47 · fever and belly pain, gallbladder out at CarePlus three days ago
cb_verghese_history.opening: Ask. Properly. CarePlus asked me four questions, and two were about my insurance.

questions.ask: What operation did you have, and when?
questions.answer: Keyhole gallbladder, at CarePlus, three days ago. Home the same evening, with a leaflet and a number that rings for ever.
questions.fact: Keyhole gallbladder at CarePlus three days ago, home the same day
questions.why: Pain and fever days after a gallbladder operation means a leak or an infection inside until proven otherwise.

questions.ask: Where is the pain, and is it getting worse?
questions.answer: It started under my right ribs. Now it's everywhere. Worse every hour. I counted. Fourteen hours.
questions.fact: Pain spreading over the whole belly, worse each hour
questions.why: Pain that spreads and keeps worsening isn't wound pain. Something is irritating the whole belly.

questions.ask: Are you allergic to anything?
questions.answer: Penicillin. I swell up. I told CarePlus. It's on their form. I filled in their form twice.
questions.fact: Allergic to penicillin: she swells up
questions.why: The usual antibiotic for a belly operation, co-amoxiclav, is a penicillin. Theatre must know before she's asleep.

questions.ask: Have you had a fever, or shivers?
questions.answer: Thirty-nine last night. I shook so hard the bed moved. My husband thought it was an earthquake.

questions.ask: Have your eyes or skin turned yellow?
questions.answer: My colleague says I look like a highlighter. She isn't a kind colleague, but she's accurate.

questions.ask: What colour is your urine?
questions.answer: Dark. Like the tea in the bank canteen. Strong enough to stand a spoon in.

questions.ask: Why did you choose CarePlus?
questions.answer: The advertisement. A smiling woman in a garden. There was no garden.

questions.ask: What do you do at the bank?
questions.answer: Cashier. Twenty-two years. I have never been short by a single rupee.

cb_grace_history.about: 56 · pain under the right ribs for a month, fever last night
cb_grace_history.opening: Go on. Ask. I'll mark you out of ten. Silently.

questions.ask: Tell me about the pain. Where is it, and when does it come?
questions.answer: Under my right ribs, after meals. Fatty ones. For a month. I've been eating less fried food and blaming the canteen.
questions.fact: Pain under the right ribs after fatty meals, for a month
questions.why: Pain under the right ribs after fatty food is the gallbladder's story: stones.

questions.ask: Do you take anything that thins the blood?
questions.answer: Aspirin. A small one every morning, since my father's heart. I took it at six today. Don't look at me like that.
questions.fact: Takes aspirin daily, took it at six this morning
questions.why: Aspirin makes the liver bed ooze. The team needs to know, and keep blood ready.

questions.ask: Have you had a fever, or turned yellow?
questions.answer: A fever last night, thirty-eight and a half. Not yellow. I checked in the sluice mirror.
questions.why: Fever means the gallbladder is inflamed now, not just full of stones. It needs to come out, not wait for a list.

questions.ask: Are you allergic to anything?
questions.answer: Nothing. Thirty-four years on the wards. I've been splashed with everything.

questions.ask: When did you last eat?
questions.answer: A biscuit at eleven last night. Priya made me eat it. She stood over me.
questions.fact: A biscuit at eleven last night

questions.ask: Have you been sick?
questions.answer: Twice. Quietly. In the staff toilet, which I cleaned afterwards.

questions.ask: Who's covering the ward?
questions.answer: That isn't a medical question. ...Tom. On a chair. God help us.

questions.ask: When did you last take a holiday?
questions.answer: Six years ago. Goa. It rained. I came back early.
